[QUERENT] Mapping Manuscript Migrations

[SYSTEM] Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) is an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV-L1G1zWsKTcIMUl26s2CYS1WC-nLTknJcEXKGVRg3SR18sDkISCW-QchbJ6PSHqNfMF_mUwT70pfkdS5HEmYBhVOxTJ2cLfoElevHNjt9rSEAnkmA03zBz-_k4EbEI917Eky), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHrOzAVhiimUeIBTse6JWvsBmsU24mXHagnL86aMRmjbyJGZCOFD7-vYmw7Ljh9-LM1mteFS0mFmQ97CFH0vmB35jt2Ad7eFpcK_bEDkjkV3eA0vq8GMSI5jwd1SotonlHnHSTgVSRLm01Qlg)]
Core Overview

* Objective & Scale: Traces the global journey of over 215,000 historical manuscripts from their creation to modern collections, enabling analysis from individual manuscript lifecycles to macro-level trade and collection trends. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHrOzAV9BINJaAaGTfKDbBNmIRJ8cjfAGJ4bc3FUVbxxVTQp1CvkYLWSjtY0RtfuBiDAACnQj_Hz5fhY9oY-qRdz_KsGbIRZA9sRcYv3ufQiSTBYFJ7ueTWnLg4HYYasLzXPI7jXDRrVacPGdIpsdyq1rBBk7Gn), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVFVwnPxxYhckZeDS2BUD8aXaAi4K17ZolyQzC40Avsmeq-Qhd7QK4kRCYvWBp2ZxFe2hNdBaTANODbzmEc3HxYg3_DhqfmNx99Q2x6O264S_L09cnDV1aqq9htfwr3M8mVrLtnU23rpOh_w), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHrOzAVhiimUeIBTse6JWvsBmsU24mXHagnL86aMRmjbyJGZCOFD7-vYmw7Ljh9-LM1mteFS0mFmQ97CFH0vmB35jt2Ad7eFpcK_bEDkjkV3eA0vq8GMSI5jwd1SotonlHnHSTgVSRLm01Qlg)]
* Partners & Funding: A collaboration between the University of Pennsylvania, University of Oxford, Institut de recherche et d'histoire des textes (IRHT-CNRS), and Aalto University, funded by the Trans-Atlantic Platform’s Digging into Data Challenge. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVmBjuFIT9rydIIXbC770wmUabUPGoHPr4yK-vGLkAJZ06_B8qUFNMyGvUVGtvXd6fSouJbWngKjR8F0BFEmx7Ivw-39uRZy58qcy6tc8s7f7t1IC1Z6noyh70B3S4D8o), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV-L1G1zWsKTcIMUl26s2CYS1WC-nLTknJcEXKGVRg3SR18sDkISCW-QchbJ6PSHqNfMF_mUwT70pfkdS5HEmYBhVOxTJ2cLfoElevHNjt9rSEAnkmA03zBz-_k4EbEI917Eky)]

Unified Datasets & Access
The project merges records from the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, and the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue into a Linked Open Data knowledge graph. Researchers can explore and query the data via the project's semantic portal and LDF.fi. transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: MAPPING MANUSCRIPT MIGRATIONS, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts.' Scale ('over 215,000 historical manuscripts'), partners (Penn, Oxford, IRHT-CNRS, Aalto) and funding (the Trans-Atlantic Platform's Digging into Data Challenge), and the merged sources (the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue') as a linked open data knowledge graph, queryable through the portal and LDF.fi. Six cards: the GitHub page, the Journal of Open Humanities Data (2020), EADH, the University of San Diego, the Zenodo record of the knowledge graph, Goldsmiths Research Online.
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview gives the project's aim, scale, partners, funder and the three databases it joins, and says where the data can be queried.
findings: THE PROJECT HELD. Partners and funder are the record's; the aggregation of three databases into linked open data is its self-description. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

THE COUNT. 'over 215,000' follows the San Diego card ('more than 215,000 medieval'); the record's white-paper figures are 217,700 manuscripts and other entities in the portal and 262,000 source records combined.

ONE SOURCE SHORTENED. The record names the three sources as 'the Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts, Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries, and Bibale'; two of the composition's cards (GitHub, San Diego) call the third 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue at the University of Oxford', and the composition drops 'at the University of Oxford'. (Repaired 2026-10-29: the finding had read it as the record's name with Oxford dropped.)

WHAT IS NOT GIVEN. The licence (CC BY-NC 4.0), on the data-paper card, is absent; the Zenodo copy of the dataset appears as a card. The project's term (funded 2017–2020) is on no card, only in the white paper the composition did not surface. (Repaired 2026-10-29: the finding had counted the term among what the cards offered.)
analysis: An aggregator of provenance is composed with its sources and partners right and its own state and terms of reuse left out: a reader cannot tell from the composition that the project ended in 2020, a fact on no card, or that its data are licensed for non-commercial reuse, a fact on one. The grain is the project's own description; the record's lifecycle and licence fields carry what the composition does not.
per_note: Penn, Oxford, IRHT-CNRS and Aalto named; no person; no identifier; the project's own GitHub page and data paper cited.
